_comment: An example profile for a DevOps / SRE / platform / cloud engineer. Copy it to config/profile.json and edit, or start from config/profile.example.json (full-stack). profile.json is gitignored — it holds your CV-level facts, which do not belong in a public repository. Every gate and weight below is read at runtime.
name: Your Name
_fieldComment: Your field in a few words. Told to the model as part of who you are.

contact._comment: Sent only in the User-Agent to the job APIs, so an operator can reach a human if a poll misbehaves. Nothing else reads it.

location._reachesComment: Named in the AI prompt when your radius crosses a border worth mentioning, e.g. "Basel (Switzerland)". Omit if it does not.
location._radiusComment: Onsite and hybrid roles must fall inside this radius. The gazetteer in src/geo.js covers Germany, Switzerland and eastern France; add coordinates there if you live elsewhere.
location._localTermsComment: Region and neighbour names that mean 'near enough' when a posting location cannot be resolved to coordinates. The city and country are added automatically; list only what they miss.

workRights._comment: Feeds the AI adjudicator so it does not surface roles you cannot legally take. Only `sponsorshipFreeIn` is read.
workRights.residence: Describe your right to work, e.g. 'EU citizen' or 'permanent resident'

languages._stretchComment: false = a stated B2 requirement is a plain drop. Set true to surface B2 roles in their own Stretch band instead. Postings that never state a requirement are judged on their own merits either way, not on the language they are written in.
languages._comment: Raise germanLevel after an exam and every gap is re-measured — 'conversational' postings promote themselves out of the Stretch band.

targetTitles._comment: STRONG = the roles you actually want, each in both engineer and architect form. canonicalTitle() folds developer/entwickler/ingenieur -> engineer, so 'DevOps Developer' and 'Cloud Ingenieur' match too.
targetTitles._goodComment: Near-identical roles posted under a different name. Kept at reduced weight so they surface without competing with the targets above.
targetTitles._excludeComment: Matched as whole words, never substrings — 'intern' will not hit 'International', 'sales' will not hit 'Salesforce'.

_searchQueriesComment: What the keyword APIs (Adzuna, JSearch, Arbeitsagentur, the agencies, the remote boards) are asked for. Absent, targetTitles.strong is used.

relevance._comment: The title vocabulary of your field. domainTerms keep a title that matches no target; offTrack drops a title as another specialisation (unless it also names a domain term — then it is a question for the model); nearMissTerms beside a role noun make a title worth asking about; nearMissPatterns are regexes for near misses a word list cannot express; roleDescription names the field in questions to the model.
relevance._nearMissComment: Keep generic words such as "operations" and "systems" OUT of this list: they pulled in "People Operations Specialist" and "Casual Rugby Systems Operator".

skills._comment:
What you work with, on two axes at once.
KIND says what sort of thing a term is (the stack gate that read it as evidence was removed 2026-10-20):
  tools      — products you can point at. Naming one is checkable.
  practices  — what those products are used for. Real, but every advert claims them.
  adjacent   — scored, but NEVER evidence. Role names ("SRE", "platform engineering")
               appear in a posting's own title and would just repeat the relevance gate.
               Programming languages are scored lightly, never wanted for themselves. Domains and outcomes
               ("GxP", "FinOps") describe a sector, not the work.
TIER decides how much a mention is WORTH when scoring: core 3.2, secondary 1.1, nice 0.5.
The two axes are independent, which is why this is nested rather than two flat lists —
they used to be exactly that, and 40 of 65 terms were duplicated between them.

domainBonus._comment: Industries your experience transfers to. Set terms to [] to switch this off.

llm._comment: LLM adjudication for the postings the rules cannot settle. Rules handle certain keeps and certain drops for free; only genuine ambiguity costs a call. Verdicts are cached by fingerprint, so re-runs are free. With no credentials the pipeline falls back to rules verdicts and says so in the report.
llm._providerComment: Gemini is the only provider. Leave `providers` null to use the .env value; set it here to override per-project.
llm._maxCallsComment: A CIRCUIT BREAKER, not a budget. At ~$0.0003 a call and about 39 calls in a typical run, cost is ~$0.36 a month — the cache absorbs 80% of escalations. 300 is roughly double the busiest real run, so it never fires normally; it exists to stop a gate regression that makes all 6,600 postings uncertain. Nothing is lost when it fires: the overflow defers to data/pending.json and is retried next run, today first.

avoid._comment: Hard exclusions on the SHAPE of the role. penaltyNiceToHaveProgramming scores down an advert that mentions coding as a nice-to-have — useful for an operations-leaning role, leave it out for a developer role.

filters._excludeEmploymentTypesComment: Canonical kinds, not source spellings: part-time, contract, internship, temporary. The gate normalises Vollzeit / Full Time / FullTime / Teilzeit / parttime etc. A value offering BOTH ("Full or part time") is never excluded.
